_doc: Per-topic KNOWN ELIGIBLE MISSING trials, populated from the adversarial audit record. Each entry names a trial the audits identified as eligible under the topic's registered PICO yet NOT in the pool, with the recovery MECHANISM that should retrieve it (vocabulary / concept-query / registry-geography / no-PMID / reference-seeding / domain-screening / access-tier). This is an invalidation trigger: a topic with a known eligible missing trial is STALE (its pooled result and completeness claim cannot be current). Trial identifiers are being externally verified against CT.gov/PubMed/EuropePMC by a read-only session; entries carry status=audit_identified until a citation lands, per our law that an unverified signal reads NOT OBSERVED, never SAFE. A named-but-unverified missing trial still invalidates the completeness claim.

superseded_note.note: VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE (PMID 23992557): population is ACUTE (first-episode) pericarditis, NOT the recurrent-pericarditis population of this topic; and the audit-cited counts 11/120 vs 25/120 (9.2%/20.8%) do NOT match the abstract (primary incessant-or-recurrent ~37.5% placebo, symptom persistence 19.2%). superseded_note.why: its population claim ('ACUTE (first-episode) pericarditis, NOT the recurrent-pericarditis population of this topic') contradicted the registered protocol, which includes acute first episodes; the same page's caveat and ledger said ICAP is eligible and not refused for population (V1.0.1 screening roles: OMISSION_VS_RECORD / OMISSION_VS_PROTOCOL)

sacubitril-valsartan-hfref.design: double-blind (registry masking TRIPLE); randomised 365; principal analysis n=335 -- a COVID-related cohort restriction, NOT all randomised (registry: 'Population was reduced due to impact of COVID-19 by removing patients with inadequate follow-up after Feb 29th, 2020.'); 24 weeks

sacubitril-valsartan-hfref.design_note: PRINCIPAL ANALYSIS n=335 of 365 randomised: a COVID-related cohort restriction, NOT all randomised. NOT POOLED: its CV death or HF hospitalisation is reported in eTable 4 of Supplement 2, which is not held; relayed (not data): 48/167 vs 37/168, HR 1.32 (0.86-2.03). Distinct outcomes in the same table, never substituted: first HF hospitalisation HR 1.24 (0.80-1.93); total HF hospitalisations 61 vs 50 EVENTS, rate ratio 1.23 (0.85-1.79) -- recurrent events, not patients. Diagnostic only (relayed): the 3-trial pool with LIFE would be 0.9724 (0.5024-1.8820) vs the served k=2 estimate. HARMS held (registry results, n 167 vs 168): 'Tolerability as measured by number of subjects developing hypotension (SBP ≤ 85 mmHg) with symptoms' 29 vs 20 (registry OR 1.55); 'Tolerability as measured by number of subjects developing moderate (\>/= 5.5 mmol/L-5.9 mmol/L) or severe (\>/= 6 mmol/L) hyperkalemia' 28 vs 15 (OR 2.05).
